problems.title: Theorem 5.2's nonuniform pairwise hitting times and inverse-rate assignment are inconsistent
source_locators: Trace clock and Skorohod convergence, pp.9-10
hypotheses: q=4; p=1/2; periodic torus with 11<=K<L=K+1
Choose sufficiently large fixed K from the asserted prefactor asymptotics, then beta->infinity
kappa1=kappa3=u>0, kappa2=v>0; stated rate to adjacent spins 1/u, opposite spin1/v
Original accelerated hitting time dominates trace hitting time pathwise
problems.decisive_evidence: The exact killed-generator equations give adjacent mean x=u(u+3v)/(2(u+v)), opposite mean y=2uv/(u+v). Thus x-u=u(v-u)/(2(u+v))>0 for sufficiently large fixed K because (5.3) yields u->3/8, v->1/2. Trace weak convergence and Fatou require the limiting original mean >=x, contradicting (5.2)'s value u. Limiting x=45/112>3/8=42/112. No exchange of K and beta limits or uniform-integrability assumption.
problems.independent_computation: independent_checks_initial.py exact2x2 solve; independent_checks_complete.py independently constructed full4x4 generator and exact killed3x3 inverse. Analytic time-change/Fatou proof in report.
problems.counterevidence: Equal off-diagonal rates do have pairwise mean equal to reciprocal rate. This covers the principal uniform-rate cyclic setting and supplies no contradiction there. The all-other-states exit mean alone matches the asserted total rate.
problems.core_dependency: Additional-model effective Markov chain, EK law, prefactor formula and comparison Remark5.3.
problems.repair: Derive a consistent effective generator and solve -Qg=1 for each target; or retain hitting constants and separately derive rates. The present contradiction alone does not identify which of the three asserted components should be replaced.
problems.impact_boundary: Joint theorem assertion in Theorem5.2 false; no disproof of main MH/p=1 cyclic results. Theorem5.2's individual components are not separately adjudicated.

problems.title: The directed Ising rates printed in Section5.2 do not preserve the Gibbs measure
source_locators: Gibbs invariance assertion and Theorem5.4, p.20
hypotheses: q=2 encoded as +/-1; K=11,L=12 periodic torus; unordered disagreement Hamiltonian
All positive spins except negative sites (4,5),(5,5),(5,6),(6,5)
Printed c_p=exp[-beta(p A+(1-p)B)] with A=NE energy increment,B=SW increment
Any beta>0 and0<p<1,p!=1/2; explicit rational check p=1/3,beta=3log2
problems.decisive_evidence: Full132-site increment multiplicities: (-2,0):2,(0,-2):1,(0,0):1,(0,2):4,(2,-2):1,(2,0):3,(2,2):120. With t=exp(beta p),u=exp(beta(1-p)), the incoming-minus-outgoing flux divided by mu(sigma) equals -(t^2-1)(t^2-u^2)(u^2-1)/(t^2u^2), nonzero in stated range. Rational out255/8,in/mu645/16,residual/mu135/16.
problems.independent_computation: Independent local-spin Fraction calculation and separate whole-Hamiltonian before/after calculation at every site; exact symbolic factorization in initial/complete check scripts. Source image confirms single exponential and no positive part.
problems.counterevidence: p=0,1 satisfy global balance by translation; p=1/2 satisfies detailed balance. Reference[19] supports pure NE/SW rates; its exponential interpolation(2.30) is one-dimensional. A convex mixture of endpoint rates would be Gibbs-stationary but defines a different process. Usual heat-bath and exponential-half-energy rates differ.
problems.core_dependency: Invariant measure and Gibbs potential theory for the additional directed-model derivation preceding Theorem5.4.
problems.repair: Analyze the actual invariant measure of the printed rates, or explicitly change generator and rederive barrier/time scaling/prefactors. An exponential mixture cannot silently be read as a convex mixture of exponentials.
problems.impact_boundary: False Gibbs assertion and invalid core premise demonstrated for this extension, including arbitrarily large beta. The residual alone does not refute every numerical assertion in Theorem5.4. Main MH and pure cyclic invariant measures are valid.
